## Question

State the question, the quantity of interest, the cost measure and the
accuracy that would answer it. Quote the operating point: time
...{claim:t_final}, budget ...{claim:target}, and the reference
concentrations ...{claim:y1_ref}, ...{claim:y2_ref}, ...{claim:y3_ref}.

## Scales and estimate

The scales of the three concentrations, the time scales of the reactions,
the Jacobian's stiff eigenvalue ...{claim:lambda_40}, and your estimate of
BS3(2)'s steps from stability, written before any run:
...{estimate:bs_steps}.

## Model and assumptions

The kinetics, the reference and how you bounded its error, the cost
measure and what it leaves out, the tolerance ladder and atol.

## Method choice

For each method its tolerance, error, steps and cost; the two costs and the
ratio in one paragraph; your choice. Why the explicit method costs what it
does: its steps at two very different tolerances, in one paragraph.

## Verification

Are the integrators right? Observed orders with their range; the explicit
step next to the stability boundary, in one paragraph; mass conservation.

## Validation

Are the results physically possible? What happens with atol = rtol = 1e-4,
in one paragraph, and why the controller did not notice.

## Uncertainty and sensitivity

The margins under the budget; the slower reactions, their stiffness, the
costs and whether the conclusion holds, in one paragraph.

## Claims and limits

Your claims, the evidence for each, the limitations, and the range where
the conclusion was tested, in one paragraph. Nothing beyond it.
